title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: a delete with dropStorage drops an object's table only with its last stored row, refused 409 while another row remains
body:
Fixes #23415
Clause-②: no

## What this does

`deleteMetaItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) now decides the table drop once, before anything is written. A delete with `dropStorage` that would leave another stored row of the object (another package's row, or the package-less row) is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. Nothing is deleted. The message gives the way out first: send the delete without `dropStorage`, or delete the other rows first and drop the table with the last one. Then it names the rows that remain.

The decision reads the rows the delete's own address read already holds (`packagelessAddress`, from the package-axis work in PR #23290 / PR #23408). It adds no second row lookup. The "what remains" values the receipt used are hoisted to the decision point, and the drop call site reads the one verdict (`dropsStorage`). The refusal is rethrown as is from the delete's `catch`, like the package-less ambiguity refusal, so it is never re-wrapped as a failed delete.

This is the seat's chosen remedy (a loud refusal, not "skip the drop and say so in the receipt"). An explicit `dropStorage=true` that drops nothing would be an opt-in the runtime does not honour while the receipt answers success.

## Measured

On the real stack: better-sqlite3 `:memory:` tables, real `ObjectQL`, real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, real REST routes. Packages `com.probe.p` and `com.probe.q` each hold a row of `probe_ticket`, and one record exists. The request is `DELETE /api/v1/meta/object/probe_ticket?package=com.probe.p&dropStorage=true`.

| | before (base `04a31487`, pin red) | after |
|---|---|---|
| status | `200`, receipt: "Deleted object 'probe_ticket' (package=com.probe.p), and it still exists: its row bound to package 'com.probe.q' remains." | `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` |
| stored active rows | `[com.probe.q]` | `[com.probe.p, com.probe.q]` |
| table exists | `false` (Q's record gone) | `true`, record `kept` still there |
| P's row plus a package-less row | rows `[null]`, table `false` | `409`, rows and table unchanged |

The refusal as served:

```text
Send the delete again without dropStorage to remove this row and keep the table, or delete the object's other rows first and drop the table with the last one. Nothing was deleted. After this delete (package=com.probe.p), object 'probe_ticket' is still served: its row bound to package 'com.probe.q' remains, and the object's records are in its table. dropStorage drops an object's table only with the object's last row.
```

## Which rows count (the reading the guard is based on)

- **Only active rows.** The guard runs only where `shouldDropStorage` says yes, and that already requires `active`. The rows it reads are the active rows at the delete's address. A draft is never materialised or served, so it holds no records. A delete of the last active row with `dropStorage` still drops the table even if another package holds only a draft. That behaviour is unchanged.
- **A package-less row counts.** A package-less row beside the deleted package's row serves the object over the same table, so it counts as a remaining row (pinned).

## Premise check: no new error code

`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409 is the standard catalog's "generic resource conflict" (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`). It is also the code the package-less ambiguity refusal answers for the same rows (`packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal`, PR #23290). The refusal comes from environment state, not from the request body: the same request is accepted once the other rows are gone. That is the case this code covers. No code is minted, and no spec, ledger or error-code file changes.

## A second door reaches the same refusal: uninstall

`deletePackage` (the uninstall) deletes each of the package's rows with `packageId` set and, unless `keepData` is set, with `dropStorage: true`. Before this change, uninstalling P from an object P and Q both hold dropped Q's table through the same call. I measured the uninstall in process on the same stack: `protocol.deletePackage({ packageId: 'com.probe.p' })` with no `keepData`.

- **Now:** `success: false`, `failedCount: 1`, and `failed[0]` carries this refusal (`code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT`). P's row of the object stays, and the table and its record stay. This is how `deletePackage` already reports any per-item refusal (its `failed[]` contract).
- **Before:** the per-item delete is the call measured above, so it dropped the table.

The new answer is safer than the data loss it replaces. It is still a partial uninstall: with a `package` service registered, the `sys_packages` row is deleted before the per-item loop, so the package's row of the shared object is left behind. The refusal's text also names `dropStorage`, which an uninstall request never sends. Changing that shape means changing `deletePackage`, which is outside this card's file surface (see Acceptance notes).

## Tests

Head `8a7b08b392` (the fix plus one merge of `origin/main` at `05ab9ef895`). The metadata-protocol and rest suites were re-run on that head after the merge. The objectql suite, the typechecks and the ablation ran on the pre-merge head `dce4a7ea77`. The merge brought no change to `protocol.ts`, `packages/rest` or the delete path: it touched objectql's lookup integrity and spec page parsing.

- New pin, `packages/rest/src/meta-delete-drop-storage-other-rows.test.ts`, on the real stack, 5 cases:
  - (a) on a control-plane kernel AND an environment kernel, `?package=P&dropStorage=true` is refused 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, the message names Q, and both rows, the table and Q's record stay;
  - a package-less remaining row is refused the same way;
  - (b)+(c) without `dropStorage`, P's delete is unchanged: `200`, the receipt names Q, the table and record stay. Then Q's delete (the last row) with `dropStorage` drops the table;
  - a single-package control: `?package=P&dropStorage=true` drops the table.
- Red at base: 3 failed, 2 passed (the two controls). Green after the fix: 5 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test`: 235 files passed (3 skipped), 28385 tests passed. After the merge: 28389 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test`: 415 files passed, 8087 tests passed. The protocol delete tests live here.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test`: 282 files passed, 5850 tests passed (326 skipped). The same after the merge.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck` (tsc plus `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0. `tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new test.
- `@objectstack/cli` was not run. `os meta delete` has no `dropStorage` flag on purpose, and `delete-reset-carriers.test.ts` pins that the flag is absent, so no CLI test reaches this path.

**Ablation (one run).** The test imports `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` through its `dist/` (`KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS`), so each leg rebuilt it and checked the marker in `dist/` before the run.

- **Mutated leg:** `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the guard `if (dropsStorage && remains) {` with a condition that never holds for a real name. The anchor count went 1 to 0 and the blob went `4d93ece86aea` to `79bb58a95ed6`. `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` found the marker in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`. The pin went red: 3 failed (the three refusal cases), 2 passed (the controls).
- **Restore leg:** the blob is back to the HEAD blob `4d93ece86aea` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. After a rebuild, `--absent` confirmed the marker is gone from all 24 built files and the tree is clean. The pin is green, 5 passed.

## Gates (local subset)

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 65 commands at head `8a7b08b392`. I ran all 65 there, unlocked, capturing each exit code before any pipe: 65 exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: "65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".

An earlier run of the same list at `9534b10c1` had three non-zero results. All three were fixed or explained before the final run:
- `check:rest-log-spy-declared` (exit 1) was a real finding: the first version of the pin spied on `console.warn`. The spy was removed.
- `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (exit 3) could not reach its pinned fixture commit on this shallow clone. It passes once that commit is fetched.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3) was PREREQUISITE NOT MET: some packages had no `dist/`.

CI runs everything outside this subset: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core.

## Acceptance notes

- **Pin placement.** The claim names `protocol-delete-object-registry-heal.test.ts` (PR #23408's `twoPackageObject`) or a sibling. That fixture's engine double has no tables and no `dropObjectSchema`, so "Q's records survive" would rest on a hand-modelled drop there. The pin therefore lives beside the REST delete door's real-stack tests (`meta-draft-head-package-inheritance.test.ts` is the harness it mirrors), on a real SQLite table. No production file outside the claimed drop region changed.
- **Spec text.** `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema.dropStorage`'s description (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) still lists only the type, state and `sys_` conditions. It does not name this refusal. The claim scoped that file to the skip remedy only, so it is untouched here. The in-code JSDoc on `deleteMetaItem`'s `dropStorage` names the refusal. Carrier: the next PR that touches `protocol.zod.ts`'s delete request.
- **Uninstall shape.** See above. Whether `deletePackage` should refuse the whole uninstall before its first durable step, or skip the drop for a shared object and say so, is a decision about `deletePackage`. It is outside this card's file surface and is raised in the dev report.
- **Legacy raw-engine path.** The drop's second call site (the legacy raw-engine delete path) is unchanged. `object` is `allowRuntimeCreate: true`, so an object delete always takes the repository path. The legacy path reaches only code-only types, which `shouldDropStorage` already rules out.
